headline: SAFF & Co. leads local rivals on review volume and holds a solid 4.3 rating, but its most-reviewed scent (S.O.T.B) is also its lowest-rated, and packaging and longevity are the pain points to watch.
kpis_note: Awareness and NPS need a consumer survey; they are not measured from public web data.

insights.text: SAFF has the most Female Daily reviews of the brands tracked (1,746 on its top 16 products vs 1,537 for HMNS) with a 4.32 weighted rating, second only to Alchemist (4.46).
S.O.T.B holds a third of SAFF's Female Daily reviews but rates 4.1, the lowest in the line along with Ostara and SAFF. The hero product pulls the brand average down.
Packaging shows up as a pain point: a 2026 review says the new bottle is too big to carry and the old one leaked.
Retailers are publishing content about SAFF 'fading fast' and about fakes, a sign that longevity and authenticity questions recur among shoppers.

recommendations.text: Dig into S.O.T.B low-star reviews (marketplace export) to find whether the issue is scent, longevity or batch, then fix copy, sampling or formula.
Add a travel or slim bottle option and check leak complaints with QC; packaging is the clearest experience gap.
Publish 'how to make it last' and 'how to spot a fake' content on product pages and inserts, to get ahead of longevity and authenticity doubts.
Run a short quarterly survey (awareness, consideration, NPS) so the report covers all brand health KPIs, not only online sentiment.
